studies.title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice.
evidence_quotes: Here we report that rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway, extends median and maximal lifespan of both male and female mice when fed beginning at 600 days of age. On the basis of age at 90% mortality, rapamycin led to an increase of 14% for females and 9% for males.

studies.title: Metformin potentiates nephrotoxicity by promoting NETosis in response to renal ferroptosis.
evidence_quotes: we treated mice with AKI induced by renal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) with different drugs alone. Notably, nicotinamide, resveratrol, rapamycin, and senolytics, but not metformin, showed some to no protective effects on AKI based on various readouts of renal health and func- tion
a higher dose of metformin (200 mg/kg) resulted in 100% lethality of I/R mice while the untreated I/R mice showed 100% survival

studies.title: The mTOR pathway is necessary for survival of mice with short telomeres.
evidence_quotes: 3-month-old wild type and second-generation telomerase-deﬁcient mice (G2 Terc−/−) in a C57BL/6 genetic background14 were fed with either control chow or chow- containing encapsulated rapamycin at 42 ppm (mg of drug per kg of food)31.

We found that rapamycin treatment increased median longevity of wild-type mice (Terc+/+) by 39%, resulting in a median longevity of 26.5 months in rapamycin-fed Terc+/+ mice compared to only 19 months in the control-fed cohorts (Fig. 1b).

studies.title: High-content screening identifies ganoderic acid A as a senotherapeutic to prevent cellular senescence and extend healthspan in preclinical models.
evidence_quotes: As expected, rapamycin (100 μM) signiﬁcantly extended the median (12%) and maximum lifespan (25%) of C. elegans (Fig. 2e).

Upon stimulating aged worms at 30 °C, treatments with rapamycin and GAA extended the mean lifespan by 23% and 35% and the maximum lifespan by 9% and 12% respectively, compared to those treated with DMSO treatment (Fig. 2f).

studies.title: Lifespan-extending interventions induce consistent patterns of fatty acid oxidation in mouse livers.
evidence_quotes: In this LC-M001 experiment, 48 mice were either untreated (Control) or subjected to one of three lifespan- extending drug treatments (ACA, 17aE2, or Rapa)

ACA, 17aE2, and Rapa showed signiﬁcantly higher RCI median in the examined modules compared to Control (Fig. 2a, Supplementary Fig. 1a), suggesting general tightening of module proﬁles by each of these lifespan-extending interventions.

studies.title: Long-lasting geroprotection from brief rapamycin treatment in early adulthood by persistently increased intestinal autophagy.
evidence_quotes: In mice, a 3-month, early treatment also induced a memory effect, with maintenance similar to chronic treatment, of lysozyme distribution, Man2B1 level in intestinal crypts, Paneth cell architecture and gut barrier function, even 6 months after rapamycin was withdrawn.
In Drosophila, a brief, early rapamycin treatment of adults extended lifespan and attenuated age-related decline in the intestine to the same degree as lifelong dosing.

studies.title: Inhibition of S6K lowers age-related inflammation and increases lifespan through the endolysosomal system.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin treatment also elevated Syntaxin 12/13 levels in mouse liver and prevented age-related increase in noncanonical NF-κB signaling

Suppression of TORC1 signaling genetically or pharmacologically by the US Food and Drug Administration-licensed drug rapamycin (Rapa), promotes lifespan and healthspan in various model organisms including nematode worms, fruit flies and mice

studies.title: The geroprotectors trametinib and rapamycin combine additively to extend mouse healthspan and lifespan.
evidence_quotes: We measured the survival of mice on diets contain- ing only rapamycin (42 mg kg–1), the dose so far inducing the largest increase in longevity20, or both rapamycin (42 mg kg–1) and trametinib (1.44 mg kg–1).

intermittent rapamycin treatment extended lifespan in both sexes to a similar extent (P < 0.0001, log-rank test; P = 0.2481 for the sex–drug interaction, Cox proportional hazard) with an increase in median and maximum lifespan of 17.4% and 16.5%, respectively, in female mice (Fig. 2b) and 16.6% and 18.3%, respectively, in male mice (Fig. 2c).

studies.title: Rapamycin extends murine lifespan but has limited effects on aging.
evidence_quotes: we performed to determine whether rapamycin slows the rate of aging in male C57BL/6J mice.

Survival analysis applied to all treated cohorts, and lifespan extension by rapamycin was demonstrated relative to corresponding vehicle controls (Figure 1), confirming previously reported longevity effects (8–11).

studies.title: Health Effects of Long-Term Rapamycin Treatment: The Impact on Mouse Health of Enteric Rapamycin Treatment from Four Months of Age throughout Life.
evidence_quotes: At four months of age 160 mice, 80 animals per sex, began receiving mouse chow (Purina 5LG6) containing either microencapsulated rapamycin (14 ppm) or empty capsules (eudragit = control), (n = 40 animals per sex and treatment group).
Consistent with our previous findings, survival of both males and females was modestly enhanced in YF animals [35].

studies.title: Transient rapamycin treatment during developmental stage extends lifespan in Mus musculus and Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin (10 mg/kg) was administered daily in two distinct temporal windows, from postnatal day 4 to postnatal day 30 (P4‐P30), or from postnatal day 30 to postnatal day 60 (P30‐P60)
Combined data from both sexes showed a 9.6% increase in median lifespan in P4‐P30 rapamycin‐treated mice compared with control mice (treated with ethanol)

studies.title: Rapamycin doses sufficient to extend lifespan do not compromise muscle mitochondrial content or endurance.
evidence_quotes: Therefore, we tested whether rapamycin, at the same doses used to extend lifespan, affects mitochondrial function in skeletal muscle.

In agreement with the lack of change in mitochondrial components, rapamycin-treated mice had endurance equivalent to that of untreated controls, and isolated, permeabilized muscle fibers displayed similar rates of oxygen consumption.

evidence_quotes: treatment with the mTORC1 inhibitor rapamycin increased lifespan of Bmal1−/− mice by 50%

studies.title: p53 and rapamycin are additive.
evidence_quotes: Mice were fed chow containing empty Eudragit capsules (control) or capsules containing 14 ppm eRapa, the concentration previously shown to extend lifespan, delay tumor-related death, retard a number of age-related pathologies, and improve cerebral function
eRapa extended the median survival of p53+/- (520 to 582 days, p=0.0522) and p53+/+ mice (681 to 802.5 days, p=0.0013).

studies.title: SRN-901, a Novel Longevity Drug, Extends Lifespan and Healthspan by Targeting Multiple Aging Pathways.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin was mixed in food with a concentration of 14.4 ppm.
While rapamycin increased lifespan in adult mice, nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), and nicotinamide riboside (NR) did not show significant differences in median lifespan compared to placebo.

studies.title: Dose-dependent effects of mTOR inhibition on weight and mitochondrial disease in mice.
evidence_quotes: we compared the effects of dietary rapamycin at doses ranging from 14 to 378 PPM on developmental weight in control and Ndufs4 knockout mice and on health and survival in the Ndufs4 knockout model.

The highest oral dose, approximately 27-times the dose shown to extend murine lifespan, increased survival in Ndufs4 knockout mice similarly to daily rapamycin injection without observable adverse effects.

studies.title: Transient rapamycin treatment can increase lifespan and healthspan in middle-aged mice.
evidence_quotes: A brief 3-month treatment of middle-aged mice with the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin produced an immediate, persistent improvement in healthspan and increased survival, with adult-onset transient rapamycin treatment significantly extending median and maximum lifespan in male mice.
